description: How the facility's agentic features are actually used: which agents people run, on which interface, what they ask them to do, and what that costs. Three sources — OpenTelemetry from the agent CLIs (Prometheus + Loki), the AF MCP server's own metrics (Rancher Prometheus), and the wrapper records that cover agents with no telemetry of their own. Prompts, responses, shell commands and tool inputs are never collected; see docs/docs/guide-agentic-telemetry.md.

panels.description: Distinct AF users whose Claude Code or codex reported at least one session in the last day. `user` comes from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, set per session by config-agents.sh.
panels.title: Users running an agent (24h)

panels.description: Distinct users who invoked a tool on the AF MCP server — a subset of the agent users to the left: everyone here ran an agent, but plenty of agent use never touches the facility's own tools.
panels.title: Users calling AF tools (24h)

panels.description: Sessions started across every instrumented agent.
panels.title: Agent sessions (24h)

panels.description: Total tokens across all users and models. Reported by the agent, so it covers the user's own account — the facility ships no model credentials.
panels.title: Tokens (24h)

panels.description: Sum of claude_code.cost.usage. This is the agent's own estimate of what the user's account was charged, not a facility cost.
panels.title: Reported spend (24h)

panels.description: Tool invocations on the AF MCP server, all clients and origins.
panels.title: MCP tool calls (24h)

panels.description: claude_code.session.count, split by the service that reported it. `job` carries service.name; agent-wrapper.sh sets OTEL_SERVICE_NAME per agent, so an agent started through the wrapper names itself here.
panels.title: Agent sessions by agent

panels.description: Counted from the agent_run records agent-wrapper.sh writes to the pod's stdout. This is the only signal for opencode, which exports no telemetry of its own, and a cross-check on the two agents that do — a gap between this and the panel to its left means telemetry was switched off, or the agent was started by its full path.

targets.expr: sum by (agent) (count_over_time({namespace="cms", container="notebook"} | json | event="agent_run" | phase="start" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Agent launches by agent (wrapper)
AF MCP server — who connects, and from where

panels.description: Handshakes on the AF MCP server, by the agent that opened them. The name comes from the clientInfo in the MCP initialize request and is clamped to an allowlist (docker/agentic-interface/clients.py); "other" is a harness nobody has classified yet — find its real name in the audit log at the bottom of this dashboard.
panels.title: MCP sessions by client

panels.description: Where the session came from. `in_session` reached the ClusterIP Service directly, which only an AF session pod can do; `external` arrived through the JupyterHub proxy — a laptop, or an agent in a session that was pointed at the public URL.
panels.title: MCP sessions by origin

panels.description: Which harness is actually doing the work, as opposed to merely connecting.
panels.title: MCP tool calls by client

panels.description: Per-user totals on the AF MCP server.
panels.title: MCP tool calls by user (24h)

panels.description: Which facility capabilities agents reach for.
panels.title: MCP tool calls by tool (24h)

panels.description: From claude_code.tool_result events. Covers every tool the agent ran — Bash, Edit, WebFetch, and MCP tools from any server, not just the facility's. Tool *parameters* are dropped at the collector for everything except MCP tools; see apps/monitoring/alloy/values.yaml.
panels.title: Tools invoked, all agents (24h)

panels.description: From claude_code.mcp_server_connection events — including servers a user configured themselves, which is the one place they become visible. A failed connection counts here too; check `status` in the log detail.
panels.title: MCP servers connected (24h)

panels.description: claude_code.token.usage. Split by user; add `type` to the grouping to separate input, output and cache reads.
panels.title: Tokens by user

panels.description: claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision — how often users accept what an agent proposes. A useful proxy for whether agent output is landing.
panels.title: Code edits accepted vs rejected

panels.description: claude_code.lines_of_code.count, by whether the agent added or removed them.
panels.title: Lines of code changed by agents

panels.description: terminal.type as the agent detected it: `vscode` is the code-server interface, `tmux`/`xterm`-like values are a JupyterLab or SSH terminal. The clearest available answer to 'where do people run agents from'.
panels.title: Sessions by terminal (7d)

panels.description: app.entrypoint: `cli` is a terminal, `claude-vscode` the code-server extension, `sdk-*` a programmatic driver such as a jupyter-ai persona. Enabled by OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ENTRYPOINT in the managed settings.
panels.title: Sessions by entrypoint (7d)

panels.description: Per-user launches from the wrapper records, so opencode is included.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (user) (count_over_time({namespace="cms", container="notebook"} | json | event="agent_run" | phase="start" [7d])))

panels.title: Agent launches by user (7d, wrapper)

panels.description: One line per tool invocation on the AF MCP server: who, which tool, which harness, from where, and the outcome. `client_raw` is the harness's own name for itself — the way an unclassified client is identified before adding it to clients._CLIENT_PATTERNS.
panels.title: AF MCP tool calls

panels.description: The raw agent_run records from agent-wrapper.sh: agent, version, user, duration and exit code, one pair of lines per invocation.
